:::{#thm-negate-quantifiers}
#### De Morgan's laws for quantifiers

For a [set](#def-set) $S$ and a [predicate](#def-predicate) $P(x)$
whose [domain of discourse](#def-domain-of-discourse) is $S$:

$$
\ba
\neg (\forall x \in S, P(x)) &\equiv \exists x \in S, \neg P(x) \\
\neg (\exists x \in S, P(x)) &\equiv \forall x \in S, \neg P(x)
\ea
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

::: proof

1. By the definition of the [universal quantifier](#def-universal-quantifier),
   $\forall x \in S, P(x)$ is false
   exactly when $P(x)$ is false for at least one $x$ in $S$.
   By the definition of the [existential quantifier](#def-existential-quantifier),
   that is exactly when $\exists x \in S, \neg P(x)$ is true.
2. By the definition of the existential quantifier,
   $\exists x \in S, P(x)$ is false
   exactly when $P(x)$ is false for every $x$ in $S$.
   By the definition of the universal quantifier,
   that is exactly when $\forall x \in S, \neg P(x)$ is true.

:::

:::
